clue.text: Single or double-decker, possibly returning with injured airmen

parts.note: in heraldry 'or' is gold, the colour yellow

indicators.note: returning says the vehicle's name is read backwards

parts.note: a double-decker is one example of a bus

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Seemingly a choice between bus types, or a bus coming back carrying wounded RAF men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link word but is heraldry's gold. 'Returning' turns BUS into SUB, and 'injured' rearranges AIRMEN into MARINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles released the song as a single in 1966, so the title names a record.

clue.text: Cameron familiarly brought up European dodge

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: David Cameron, former UK prime minister, is familiarly called Dave

explanation.surface: A politician raises the subject of a European tax dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' turns DAVE into EVAD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid it skilfully, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Endlessly criticising e.g. Status Quo

indicators.note: endlessly means both ends of the word are cut off

parts.note: slating is informal British for harsh criticising

explanation.surface: Someone keeps knocking the rock band Status Quo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Status Quo' looks like the British rock band; it is the phrase itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase status quo comes straight from the classical Roman language, so it is an example.

clue.text: Poet's extra line inserted

indicators.note: inserted says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a kind of extra, a run not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: A poet's added line of verse slipped into the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde wrote poetry, notably The Ballad of Reading Gaol.

clue.text: America acquires first instalment of Rupert Bear

indicators.note: acquires means the country takes something in, inside its letters
the first instalment of a name is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A US buyer picks up the first episode of the Rupert Bear children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa is Latin for a she-bear, as in the constellations Ursa Major and Minor.

clue.text: Enough money to climb tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letter moves upwards, toward the top

parts.note: ample means enough or plenty
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3 money supply

explanation.surface: Enough cash to let someone go up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To climb' lifts M from inside AMPLE to its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A maple is a familiar broad-leaved tree, the source of syrup.

clue.text: Watertight, lead-free pipe initially plumbing top of house

indicators.note: lead-free means losing the leading letter

parts.note: a drain is a pipe carrying waste water

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: the roof is the top of a house

explanation.surface: A plumber's job: unleaded piping fitted to the top of a house to keep water out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' looks like the metal in old pipes; it removes the first letter of DRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resistant to rain lets no water through, a synonym.

clue.text: Hurry back with baby-carrier to restrain irrational infant

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to run is to hurry

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a sling is a fabric baby-carrier
e is the irrational number, the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A parent rushes back with a sling to hold a tantrum-throwing baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like the infant's mood; it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseling is an old word for a baby being nursed, so a synonym.

clue.text: Wearer of shell suit with an extremely unusual design

indicators.note: design means the letters are arranged into a new pattern
extremely picks the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone in a shell suit with a very odd pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a shiny nylon tracksuit; here 'shell' is the creature's own. 'Extremely' gives UL from 'unusual', and 'design' rearranges SUIT, AN and UL.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautilus is a sea mollusc living in a spiral chambered shell.

clue.text: Former axis for religious building

parts.note: prior means former or earlier
y is the vertical axis on a graph

explanation.surface: An old pivot point for a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a monastery or convent run by a prior or prioress.

clue.text: Revolutionary communist pursuing plan to change course

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after the other piece

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning the word round

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A radical leftist follows a scheme to alter the direction of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the communist, but it signals turning the word round; 'pursuing' puts it after the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A winding river keeps altering direction, the image behind the verb.

clue.text: Chief requirement for country kitchen?

definitions.meaning: a Turkish or Ottoman commander or chief
the heavy cast-iron range cooker found in British farmhouse kitchens

explanation.surface: What the head cook demands for a rustic kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga is both an Ottoman title for a commander and a brand of range stove.

clue.text: VAR's conclusion irritates team

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter

parts.note: angers means irritates

explanation.surface: The video referee's ruling infuriates a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is football's video assistant referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a Glasgow football club, as are several other teams.

clue.text: Greenpeace lashed plastic over rear of vessel — one used to plumb ocean

indicators.note: plastic means able to be moulded, so the letters are reshaped
the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The environmental group attacked plastics dumped from the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like Greenpeace's target; it reshapes GREENPEACE LASHED with L from 'rear of vessel'.
explanation.definitionFit: This submersible took James Cameron to the bottom of the Mariana Trench in 2012.

clue.text: Performed in tandem fitting concert finale alongside online lecture

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a TED talk is a famous kind of short online lecture

explanation.surface: Two musicians played together to close a concert, beside a web talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing or play as a pair is to perform a two-part piece together.

clue.text: See 14
Revealing statement of man heading to battle first

indicators.note: heading means placed at the head of the rest
first means the battle comes before the word to

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Ypres in Belgium was the site of several First World War battles

explanation.surface: Words of a soldier leading the charge into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ypres is the Belgian town of several First World War battles; 'first' sets it before the word 'to', and 'heading' sets the man in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror says it when revealing the trick, a stock exclamation.

clue.text: Give up cryptic instructions for making better beer

parts.note: the word better, losing its central TT, becomes beer

explanation.surface: Giving up on brewing instructions for an improved beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: remove the middle of 'better' and you are left with 'beer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing courage means abandoning hope, an idiom for giving up.

clue.text: State address when meeting Oscars guard

indicators.note: the two letters guard the greeting by standing either side of it

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O, so two Oscars give two Os
hi is a greeting, a way to address someone

explanation.surface: A celebrity speech when meeting security at the Academy Awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: They can see the Speaker's support for motion

indicators.note: the Speaker's version means said aloud, with a nod to the Commons Speaker

parts.note: in parliament the ayes are the votes supporting a motion

explanation.surface: Parliament's Speaker counts votes in favour of a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' looks like the Commons chair calling 'the ayes have it', but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what let creatures see.

clue.text: Spinner provided unwitting boundaries in the middle

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: the centre is the middle
if means provided that

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler gives unknowing batsmen boundaries mid-pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' and 'boundaries' suggest cricket, a spin bowler and a four or six; here 'boundaries' means the outer letters of 'unwitting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifuge spins samples at high speed to separate them, so it is a spinning machine.

clue.text: Spacecraft's periodic out-of-doors appearances

indicators.note: periodic means taking letters at regular intervals, here every third

explanation.surface: A spaceship occasionally shows itself in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every third letter of OUT-OF-DOORS, starting from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are popularly taken to be alien spacecraft.

clue.text: They appear on sprigs or sprogs, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the words are taken as said aloud

parts.note: sprogs is British slang for kids, so the words say 'or kids'

explanation.surface: Something that grows on young shoots, or on young children.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprigs and sprogs differ by one letter; a sprog is a British slang word for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: These flowers bloom on stems, so they appear on plant sprigs.

clue.text: Fantasy Island's back on This Morning?

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: re means on, concerning
am stands for morning, before noon

explanation.surface: The reality show Fantasy Island returns to ITV's daytime show This Morning.
explanation.walkthrough: This Morning is a British TV magazine show; here it gives AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy is an imagined wish, a synonym.

clue.text: Film party time being stopped by injunction

indicators.note: stopped by means the other piece plugs the gap in this one

parts.note: a do is a party
an ASBO, a British anti-social behaviour order, was a court injunction

explanation.surface: A party shut down by a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: ASBO is a British anti-social behaviour order.
explanation.definitionFit: Das Boot is a 1981 German movie about a U-boat crew.

clue.text: Neighbourhood which includes Newcastle's foremost stadium

indicators.note: includes means the other letter goes inside

parts.note: an area is a neighbourhood

indicators.note: foremost means the opening letter

explanation.surface: A district in the north-east containing Newcastle's main football ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a large venue for sport or concerts, a stadium.

clue.text: Pretend to be fit around fifty

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: buff means fit and muscular
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Claiming to be in shape at around fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around fifty' looks like an age; 'around' puts BUFF round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to deceive by feigning, so a synonym for pretend.

clue.text: Make a decision in charge of 19

definitions.note: the singular answer stands for the plural answer to 19, as one of them

parts.note: to opt is to make a decision

explanation.surface: Choose to take command of clue 19.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 19 is EYES; 'optics' is slang for eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is informal and technical for an organ of sight.

clue.text: A short excerpt of William Blake

indicators.note: excerpt of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brief passage from the poet William Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like part of 'short excerpt' but closes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This metrical foot opens with a short, unstressed syllable before a long one.

clue.text: Emanation from Earth's mantle

parts.note: E is short for Earth, plus the S of the possessive
a cape is a cloak or mantle

explanation.surface: Something given off from the layer beneath the Earth's crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mantle' looks like the geological layer; it is a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas escape is a leak, something emanating or flowing out.

clue.text: Unexceptional Russian agreement's rejected to achieve parity

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: da is Russian for yes
to equate things is to make them equal

explanation.surface: An ordinary Russian deal is thrown out so both sides are level.
explanation.definitionFit: Something merely sufficient is passable but ordinary, nothing special.

clue.text: Sir David Attenborough to launch this recycled fat and tobacco, maybe

definitions.text: Sir David Attenborough to launch this

indicators.note: recycled means the material is reused in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The naturalist promotes recycling of grease and tobacco products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir David Attenborough' is the polar research ship, not the man; the public's vote name for it went to its submersible.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar research ship carries this remote submarine, named after a public poll.
